BelOMO PK-AS

The PK-AS is a holographic collimator sight for mounting on Picatinny rail manufactured by the Belarussian company BelOMO. Originally descended from the PKS-07 magnified scope used on the SV98 and sometimes SVD Dragunov rifles, the PK-AS is the non-magnified version inspired from the original PKS-01. Due to it's construction and with its thin scope body, the edges almost completely disappear with both eyes open, leaving the user with an excellent field of view.

BelOMO PK-A (Picatinny)

The PK-A is a sturdy and robust red dot tube optic. Originally appearing to be an adaptation of the original PSO SVD optic, the PK-A has a similar construction and the same style of hammer grey finish. The newer versions use different style turrets for windage and elevation and appear to be POSP turrets, vs the original which are much smaller and not marked with numbers. Some models have been adapted to be mounted on Picatinny rails.

Elbit Falcon II

The next generation of this renowned series of holosights, the Falcon II becomes a worthy heir to the reputation of her predecessor. Many user reports asserts that first round hit probability is tremendously increased with the proper use of this reflex sight, especially on moving targets. Built like a tank to last indefinitely in the harshest conditions, many examples in The Zone show signs of intense abuse in service but remain fully functional. The downside are its considerable size and weight compared to other similar devices, which has meant that its military use has not been as widespread as that of its predecessor. But in The Zone these inconveniences are considered trivialities compared to the advantages of having a durable and effective device in an environment where it is never easy to get spare parts or replacements, which is why they are in high demand whenever one goes on sale.

Mark 4 CQ/T

The Mark 4 CQ/T is a variable 1-3x of power magnification scope developed and sold starting in the early 2000s. The scope attempted to combine the features of a red dot and low power scope in one package. While in the 2020s the idea of the LPVO is widespread, at the time few scopes intended for military use existed in this catagory. The scope has an eleven position illumination dial that is powered by a single AA battery. With a battery life was 600+ hours on a medium setting or 7 hours on the highest setting. Eye relief was designed with the M16/M4 length of pull in mind. While it did achieve some sales seeing use by multiple US military branchs and with police forces in multiple countries during the mid to late 2000s, the the Mark 4 CQ/T never achieved the success of other sights of its era like the ACOG, Eotech and Aimpoint.

LOMO PKS-07 (Picatinny)

The PKS-07 Tactical Sniper Sight is a unique sniper scope based on collimator technology. The scope was created in LOMO (Saint-Petersburg, Russia) especially for the VSK-94 sniper platform. As it was technologically more advanced as well as lighter, the Russian military has chosen it over the PSO-3 as the standard optic for the SV-98. It's fully coated prismatic lens system provides a remarkable, high contrast, wide angle field of view and lower eyepiece location for comfortable aiming. The scope has an illuminated rangefinding reticle. The scope has POSP-style windage and elevation adjustments (every elevation turret' click moves POI by 4.5 cm at 100 m, every windage turret' click moves POI by 2.5 cm at 100 m). The special protective lens coatings protect the scope from scratching and fouling in the extreme battlefield conditions where it was designed to operate. This version has been adaptad to be mounted in Picatinny rails.

AN/PSV-4 Night Scope

The AN/PVS-4 is a second generation passive Night vision device first deployed in 1978 by the US Army. Although passive night vision technology capable of allowing vision under ambient starlight conditions has existed since the 1950s, it was not until the AN/PVS-4 was developed that a practical, high-quality device that met military requirements was first made available. Unlike earlier passive starlight weapon scopes the AN/PVS-4 provided a high quality image without significant distortion, could adjust to changing ambient light conditions, was able to take multiple reticles to operate in many roles and had protective features allowing it to shut down in the event of exposure to bright light, but still recover in time after a muzzle flash for the operator to see the round hit the target. It was widely deployed on a variety of weapons during the Gulf War, which was the first war in which ground combat operations continued both day and night through the use of night vision devices. The AN/PVS-4 became one of the most widely used night vision scopes and has been in active use for more than a quarter of a century. Decommissioned examples from western armies arsenals has found their way into The Zone through weapons smugglers and although it does not offer the same image quality as other more modern devices, it is still highly sought after as it is one of the few of its kind available to the average stalker.
